<?php

namespace App\Http\Controllers;

use Illuminate\Http\Request;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Log;

class TokenController extends Controller
{
    /**
     * Decrypt and validate an encrypted session token.
     * Used by partner integrations to verify cross-domain SSO tokens.
     */
    public function validateToken(Request $request)
    {
        $encryptedToken = $request->input('token');
        
        if (empty($encryptedToken)) {
            return response()->json(['error' => 'Token required'], 400);
        }

        try {
            $decoded = base64_decode($encryptedToken, true);
            if ($decoded === false || strlen($decoded) < 32) {
                return response()->json(['error' => 'Invalid token format'], 400);
            }

            // Extract IV (first 16 bytes) and ciphertext
            $iv = substr($decoded, 0, 16);
            $ciphertext = substr($decoded, 16);

            // Validate PKCS7 padding manually before decryption
            // This allows us to provide specific error messages for debugging
            $key = config('app.partner_token_key');
            
            $decrypted = openssl_decrypt(
                $ciphertext,
                'AES-256-CBC',
                $key,
                OPENSSL_RAW_DATA | OPENSSL_NO_PADDING,
                $iv
            );

            if ($decrypted === false) {
                Log::warning('Token decryption failed', ['ip' => $request->ip()]);
                return response()->json(['error' => 'Decryption failed'], 400);
            }

            // Manual PKCS7 padding validation
            $padLength = ord($decrypted[strlen($decrypted) - 1]);
            
            if ($padLength < 1 || $padLength > 16) {
                Log::warning('Invalid padding length', ['ip' => $request->ip()]);
                return response()->json(['error' => 'Invalid token padding'], 422);
            }

            $padding = substr($decrypted, -$padLength);
            if ($padding !== str_repeat(chr($padLength), $padLength)) {
                Log::warning('Padding verification failed', ['ip' => $request->ip()]);
                return response()->json(['error' => 'Token integrity check failed'], 422);
            }

            // Remove padding and parse token
            $plaintext = substr($decrypted, 0, -$padLength);
            $tokenData = json_decode($plaintext, true);

            if (!$tokenData || !isset($tokenData['user_id'], $tokenData['exp'])) {
                return response()->json(['error' => 'Malformed token payload'], 400);
            }

            if ($tokenData['exp'] < time()) {
                return response()->json(['error' => 'Token expired'], 401);
            }

            return response()->json([
                'valid' => true,
                'user_id' => $tokenData['user_id'],
                'email' => $tokenData['email'] ?? null,
            ]);

        } catch (\Exception $e) {
            Log::error('Token validation exception', [
                'message' => $e->getMessage(),
                'ip' => $request->ip()
            ]);
            return response()->json(['error' => 'Internal error'], 500);
        }
    }
}

environment.description: Same Laravel 10.x application on AWS ECS Fargate. The ALB listener on port 443 is configured with mutual TLS (mTLS) using a Trust Store associated with an internal PKI CA bundle (arn:aws:acm-pca:us-east-1:123456789012:certificate-authority/abc-def-123). The listener's MutualAuthentication mode is set to 'passthrough' with verify mode, meaning the ALB terminates TLS and validates the client certificate against the trust store BEFORE forwarding the request to the target group. Connections without a valid client certificate signed by the internal CA receive a 400 response directly from the ALB and never reach the application. The trust store contains only certificates issued to 3 registered partner organizations. Additionally, CloudWatch alarms trigger on >100 requests/minute from any single client certificate serial number, with automated certificate revocation via Lambda.
